title: More turns on the primary
hook: Change primary turn count and predict secondary voltage magnitude.
misconception: secondary voltage magnitude doubles when primary turn count doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply Vs/Vp = Ns/Np to compare secondary voltage magnitude when primary turn count changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal transformer with fixed primary voltage and secondary turn count, Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. When primary turn count doubles, secondary voltage magnitude becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Vs/Vp = Ns/Np; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal transformer with fixed primary voltage and secondary turn count, with a nonzero initial result. If primary turn count triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on secondary voltage magnitude?
recall.why: Apply Vs/Vp = Ns/Np under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
